caption: Newanforbi v. California Highway Patrol, et al.
claims: Writ of Mandate (CCP §1085; PC §679.10) — U Visa Certification; Declaratory Relief (CCP §1060)
status: Active — Petition filed 05/29/2026; AG Demurrer (CHP) filed; Opposition to Demurrer filed 07/13/2026; CHP Demurrer Hearing: 08/28/2026, 9:00 a.m., Dept. 25 — Hon. Jenna M. Whitman. Individual Respondents Serrato, Paul, and Dutra filed their own Joinders and Demurrers 07/30/2026, each also arguing Petitioner fails to allege they are 'certifying officials' under PC §679.10(b); a Joint Stipulation filed the same day asks the Court to advance their Oct. 16/23, 2026 hearing dates to Aug. 28, 2026 to be heard alongside CHP's Demurrer — stipulation not yet signed/entered. Separately, the July 15, 2026 Case Management Conference was continued to September 2, 2026 per the court's tentative ruling (forwarded by Deputy AG Vanessa Ing).
defendants: California Highway Patrol; G. Serrato, Captain and Commander CHP Dublin Area; Gary Paul, Lieutenant CHP Dublin Area; Eric Dutra, Sergeant CHP Dublin Area; DOES 1-10
causes: Count I — Writ of Mandate (CCP §1085): Failure to Perform Mandatory Duty Under Penal Code §679.10(b) — compel certification of Form I-918 Supplement B
Count II — Writ of Mandate (CCP §1085): Failure to Perform Ministerial Duty Under PC §679.10(g) — reason-giving requirement for denials
Count III — Writ of Mandate (CCP §1085): Failure to Apply Rebuttable Presumption of Helpfulness Under PC §679.10(h)
Count IV — Declaratory Relief (CCP §1060): Facial Deficiency of April 20, 2026 Denial and Construction of PC §679.10
key_facts: On April 9, 2026, Petitioner submitted a formal request for U Nonimmigrant Status Certification (Form I-918 Supplement B) to CHP pursuant to 8 U.S.C. §1101(a)(15)(U) and California Penal Code §679.10, seeking certification as a victim of qualifying criminal activity. On April 20, 2026, eleven days later, CHP Commander G. Serrato denied the certification in a five-sentence conclusory letter that: (1) identifies no specific statutory element that Petitioner fails to satisfy; (2) does not name a single enumerated qualifying offense considered or rejected; (3) does not engage with CHP's own dashcam recording; (4) does not reconcile the conclusion with CHP's own PC §851.6 detention certificate; and (5) does not acknowledge or apply the statutory rebuttable presumption of helpfulness. Petitioner is a victim of multiple enumerated qualifying offenses under 8 U.S.C. §1101(a)(15)(U)(iii): false imprisonment/unlawful criminal restraint, felonious assault/battery, obstruction of justice, and perjury. Evidence is overwhelming: (1) CHP's own dashcam audio-video recording (November 1, 2024, I-580 East, Livermore) directly contradicts CHP's own sworn arrest report on four material points — the asserted 'strong distinct odor of an alcoholic beverage,' 'slurred' speech, 'very confused and disoriented' demeanor, and 'beverage present: yes'; (2) CHP's own PC §851.6 detention certificate (issued November 5, 2024) reclassifies the arrest as 'a detention only, not an arrest' for 'insufficient grounds for making a criminal complaint'; (3) no criminal charges were ever filed by the Alameda County DA; (4) Petitioner has fully cooperated with every investigative channel — filed citizen complaint, POST complaint, participated in DMV proceedings, obtained and produced the dashcam transcript. The statutory rebuttable presumption of helpfulness (PC §679.10(h)) attaches and is uncontroverted. CHP's April 20, 2026 denial is: (a) based on an incorrect legal standard; (b) made without applying the rebuttable presumption of helpfulness; (c) wholly unsupported by and irreconcilable with the agency's own contemporaneous documentary record; and (d) inconsistent with PC §679.10(k)'s explicit instruction that prosecution and conviction are not required.
procedural_status: Verified Petition for Writ of Mandate filed May 29, 2026, in Alameda County Superior Court (Case No. 26CV191136; designated for mandatory action under CCP §1085). June 3, 2026: Notice of E-Filing Confirmation received; Petition accepted by court; Notice of Case Management Conference issued (originally set July 15, 2026); Summons on Petition served on respondents (Serrato, Paul, Dutra, and CHP); Request to Waive Court Fees submitted. June 30, 2026: Petitioner electronically filed his Case Management Statement (Judicial Council Form CM-110). July 12, 2026: Hon. Jenna Whitman issued a Tentative Ruling re: Case Management, continuing the July 15, 2026 CMC to September 2, 2026, 4:00 PM, Dept. 25, on the ground that the pleadings are not yet at issue — Deputy AG Vanessa Ing forwarded the tentative by email as a courtesy. July 15, 2026: Case Management Conference CONTINUED to September 2, 2026 — the tentative ruling was not contested at the hearing and was affirmed; a signed Order Initial Case Management Conference issued the same day, entered and file-stamped by the Clerk July 21, 2026, with a Certificate of Electronic Service on Petitioner and DAG Vanessa Kelley Ing and a Certificate of Mailing to Petitioner's address of record. AG's Demurrer (Deputy AG Vanessa Ing) rests on a single core theory across all four counts: that certifying a Form I-918 Supplement B is a discretionary act, not a ministerial duty, so no writ of mandate can compel it under CCP §1085 regardless of the facts pled — citing Catholic Charities CYO v. Chertoff (N.D. Cal. 2008) for the proposition that federal law imposes no mandatory certification duty on law enforcement; in the alternative, the AG argues the Petition's allegations are conclusory even if a duty existed, and that no amendment could cure the defect, so the demurrer should be sustained without leave to amend. July 13, 2026: Petitioner filed Opposition to Demurrer to Petition for Writ of Mandate (with MPA), Declaration of Petitioner in Support of Opposition, Request for Judicial Notice with Exhibits, Proposed Order Overruling Demurrer, and Proof of Service — complete opposition package filed in response to AG/Deputy AG Vanessa Ing's demurrer. The Opposition's MPA argues the demurrer improperly asks the Court to resolve disputed merits facts at the pleading stage, to read AB 1261's written-explanation requirement out of PC §679.10(i)(2), and to import an agency-cooperation-request threshold into the §679.10(h) helpfulness presumption that appears nowhere in the statute's text; Petitioner does not ask the Court to order certification on the pleadings alone, but seeks judicial review of CHP's compliance with §679.10's mandatory procedures, with vacatur-and-remand as the minimum remedy. The Request for Judicial Notice asks the Court to notice, under Evid. Code §§452(c)-(d), 453: (Exhibit A) Magistrate Judge Ajay S. Krishnan's June 29, 2026 Order Re Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis in the related federal action Newanforbi v. Serrato, No. 4:26-cv-05953-ASK (N.D. Cal.) — argued as directly relevant because that order screened and found sufficient a complaint arising from this same underlying incident and the same April 20, 2026 certification denial challenged in this Petition; and (Exhibit B) Assembly Bill No. 1261 (2023-2024 Reg. Sess.), ch. 679, Stats. 2023. This is the second sibling matter (after Matter 1's July 7, 2026 Notice of Supplemental Authority) to formally cite the Krishnan/Serrato order to a court as persuasive authority. Parallel track: this same April 20, 2026 CHP denial also prompted Petitioner to file a U-Visa Certification Motion within the pending Matter 2 tort action (26CV168913), asking the Alameda Superior Court judge already presiding over that case to certify Form I-918 Supplement B directly under his own independent certifying-official authority (8 U.S.C. §1101(a)(15)(U)(i)(III); PC §679.10(a)(1)) — briefed May–June 2026, hearing June 18, 2026, Dept. 518, independent of this writ's mandamus track against CHP itself. July 24, 2026 (9:44 a.m.): Deputy AG Vanessa Ing emailed Petitioner requesting his availability to meet and confer on the Individual Respondents' (Serrato, Paul, Dutra) intended demurrers/joinders; Petitioner responded July 27, 2026 (10:13 a.m.) that he would not amend the Petition and that his already-filed Opposition applied equally to the Individual Respondents. A telephonic meet-and-confer was also held — Ing's declaration dates it 'Monday, July 26, 2026,' though July 26, 2026 is in fact a Sunday and the surrounding Friday-the-24th/Monday-the-27th sequence in the same declaration suggests this is a scrivener's error for July 27; Petitioner's position did not change either way. July 27, 2026: counsel for the Individual Respondents reserved hearing dates of October 16, 2026 (Serrato, Paul) and October 23, 2026 (Dutra) for their intended demurrers/joinders, then during that day's meet-and-confer the parties agreed in principle to instead advance both dates to August 28, 2026 to be heard together with CHP's own Demurrer. July 30, 2026: the Individual Respondents filed (1) their own Notices of Joinder to CHP's Demurrer plus separate Demurrers and supporting MPAs — each adopting CHP's core discretionary-duty theory by joinder and each raising one additional, individualized ground that the Petition fails to allege the respondent is a 'certifying official' within PC §679.10(b)(1)-(4): Dutra is alleged only as the 'assigned investigator and designated recipient on the Supplement B' (Pet. ¶16), Paul only as a 'supervisory official... with responsibility for processing the certification request' (Pet. ¶15), and Serrato — the only one of the three who actually signed the April 20, 2026 denial letter — on the same theory; each respondent requests his demurrer be sustained without leave to amend; (2) a Joint Stipulation to Advance Dates of Hearings on Demurrers of Individual Respondents with a [Proposed] Order, formalizing the July 27 agreement to move the Individual Respondents' October hearings to August 28, 2026 (not yet signed/entered by the Court); and (3) a separate [Proposed] Order Granting Joinders of Individual Respondents; Sustaining Demurrers to Petition for Writ of Mandate — a merits-ruling order drafted by the Individual Respondents for submission at that eventual hearing (also unsigned; not to be confused with the scheduling order in (2)). Demurrer Hearing: August 28, 2026, 9:00 a.m., Dept. 25, Hon. Jenna M. Whitman — currently the date reserved for CHP's Demurrer; if the pending stipulation is entered, the Individual Respondents' Demurrers and Joinders will be heard the same day. AG reply due approximately August 21, 2026 (5 court days before hearing per CRC 3.1320(b)); Trial Date: Not set. Petitioner seeks in Tier 1 (procedural relief): (a) alternative writ directing respondents to show cause; (b) peremptory writ vacating the April 20, 2026 denial; and (c) peremptory writ commanding compliance with reason-giving requirement of PC §679.10(g). In Tier 2 (standards relief): peremptory writ commanding reconsideration under correct legal standards including enumerated offenses, rebuttable presumption, no-prosecution-required rule, and consideration of agency's own evidence. In Tier 3 (substantive relief): conditional certification order if respondents cannot satisfy Tier 2 standards within specified period. Also seeks declaratory relief on statutory interpretation, evidence preservation order, retained jurisdiction for 36 months, and attorney's fees under CCP §1021.5.
damages: [FLAGGED: this CDL lost-wage figure is also independently claimed, unreserved, in Matters 1, 2, and 7 for the same one-year suspension — see the note on Matter 1's damages field] Economic: Approximately $112,000 in documented lost wages during one-year CDL suspension (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026), with continuing losses at ~$6,000/month. Wage documentation: 26 consecutive weekly Centerline Drivers LLC pay stubs (May 5, 2024 – Jan. 3, 2025) averaging $900–$2,800/week. Non-economic: Severe emotional distress and anxiety from denial of federal immigration relief avenue; complete loss of employment prospects in CDL industry; ongoing professional and reputational harm; out-of-pocket compliance and collateral costs. Total quantifiable damages exceed $112,000 with continuing accrual.
risk: Favorable case with strong documentary support. CHP's own evidence (dashcam recording and detention certificate) defeats the denial on its face. Attorney General's guidance (DLE-2024-05) mandates certification under these facts. Petitioner has clearly satisfied all three statutory elements. The only vulnerability is subject-matter jurisdiction if court deems this a federal U-visa matter — but Petitioner challenges only state-law procedural/substantive duties imposed by the Legislature, not federal adjudication of U-visa eligibility (properly before USCIS). Added July 30, 2026 vulnerability, narrower in scope: each Individual Respondent separately argues the Petition does not plead facts fitting him within PC §679.10(b)'s four-category definition of 'certifying official.' This is weakest as to Serrato, who signed the actual denial letter, and strongest as to Dutra and Paul, whose pleaded roles (assigned investigator/recipient; supervisory processing official) do not track the statute's enumerated categories (head of entity, specifically-designated supervisory designee, judge, or 8 C.F.R. §214.14(a)(2) official) on their face — a defect that, if not cured by amendment identifying the missing designation fact, could narrow the writ to CHP and Serrato even if the core discretionary-duty theory otherwise survives.
